intent.symptom_summary: The raw-mode CodeEditor uses an overlay edit mechanism (transparent textarea stacked over an aria-hidden highlighted pre, per-keystroke debounced re-tokenization, a colored snapshot shown while editing, textarea->pre scroll sync) that diverges from the design's edit/preview toggle and carries avoidable complexity (dual-layer scroll sync, debounce timing, live-vs-snapshot coloring). Change it to a design-matched editing-state toggle.
intent.desired_summary: An 'editing' boolean gates the render: editing=true shows a plain textarea (spellCheck off, resize none, native undo/selection/IME, native Tab, white-space:pre with horizontal scroll, no soft-wrap); editing=false shows the highlighted pre (preview). Never both mounted. Transitions: enter edit via (a) clicking the preview — caret MUST be placed at the clicked character position — or (b) the toggle button; leave edit (edit->preview) on BOTH textarea blur AND the toggle button. compose() tokenization runs ONCE on the switch-to-preview transition, not per keystroke. Gutter tracks whichever layer is visible within one scroll container. No colored-during-edit snapshot; no textarea->pre scroll sync.
intent.verbatim_prompt: Change the raw-mode code editor's edit mechanism from an overlay to the design's editing-toggle, in the request body editor's extracted CodeEditor molecule. Current: the CodeEditor layers a transparent textarea over an aria-hidden highlighted pre, with per-keystroke debounced re-tokenization, a colored snapshot shown while editing, and textarea->pre scroll sync. Desired: match the design -- an `editing` state that renders EITHER a plain textarea (while editing) OR the highlighted pre (preview), never both; tokenize once on switch-to-preview, not per keystroke; drop the textarea/pre scroll-sync and the live-vs-debounced colored-during-edit path. Accepted tradeoff: no syntax highlighting while typing (plain in edit, colored in preview). Behavioral contract to pin: the edit surface is a plain textarea (spellCheck off, resize none) with native undo / selection / IME; wrap is white-space pre with horizontal scroll and no soft-wrap; the Tab key stays native; the gutter tracks the visible layer within one scroll container. Out of scope, do not build: auto-indent, bracket/quote auto-close, multi-cursor, find/replace, paste-and-format, and any third-party editor engine. Unchanged, must survive: the single shared line-box unit that keeps textarea, pre, and gutter rows equal at 20.625px; reuse of the existing JSON tokenizer compose lib byte-unchanged; the malformed-JSON degrade-to-plain path; the code data-testids; the reset-on-change signal that resets scroll and invalidates the colored snapshot when the active request tab switches; and none/urlencoded mode behavior. The edit/preview toggle button is a separate concern.

risks.risk: Line-box (20.625px) alignment must hold in BOTH toggle states; gutter must track the visible layer in one scroll container; caret-at-click mapping correctness; scroll-position preservation across toggle.

plan_seeds.recommended_approach_summary: Option 1 wins on the one non-negotiable the brief states outright: at any instant the DOM must contain just one of the two surfaces, and its test hook must be the sole marker attached. Option 2 retains a dormant second surface and is excluded by that rule. Every must-not-regress item is honored — the 20.625 px row metric stays a shared constant in either state, the colouring helper is reused unmodified and fires one time on return to preview, the reset scalar's scroll-and-discard signal is kept, and the empty and form-encoded paths are untouched. Two questions stay unresolved and are logged below: retaining the viewport scroll over a state switch, and where the insertion point lands on entry from a pointer press.

alternatives_considered.summary: Keep both textarea and pre mounted at all times and toggle only their CSS visibility, reusing BodyEditor's hidden-toggle idiom (BodyEditor.tsx:171). compose() could still run once on entering preview.

discriminator.primary_confirms_if: if selectionStart == clicked char offset -> native click-through/mapping suffices (H-B benign); if it lands at 0 or text end -> a manual click-coordinate->char-offset mapping is required before focus (H-B confirmed).
